goal: Close all access-control findings and all use-case acceptance requirements

findings.description: **Unverified email can claim invitations without the token.** Signup under an unverified address, then `/me/invitations` discovers invitations for that email; `/me/invitations/{id}/accept` accepts them, including workspace admin. Email equality is not mailbox proof. `api/shared_with_me.py:261,335`; `services/invitations.py:152,517`. Probe `test_unverified_email_can_discover_and_accept_invitation_without_token`. Require verified ownership of the current email for discovery/by-ID acceptance. A valid invitation token can authorize that specific invitation under a defined bearer/recipient contract; it must not automatically verify the account email, because the issuer also receives the acceptance URL. Keep ordinary login non-blocking.
implementation: Bound server-owned verified_email and OTP delivery address to current AuthUser email
Gate by-ID invitation actions/discovery; token path does not verify account
verification: test_invitation_mailbox_proof.py: 9 HTTP/service cases; targeted selection passed

findings.description: **Entry exclusions do not protect event snapshots.** A Track viewer excluded from an Entry receives its `entry.update` event `after` payload. Broadcast authorizes only `track:<id>`. Audit and polling use the same scope-only policy dispatch, so they require equivalent repair. `event_subscription_registry.py:85,106`; `policy_engine.py:273`; `api/audit_log.py:104`; `api/events_polling.py:103`. Probe `test_entry_exclusion_does_not_filter_event_payload`. Authorize the affected resource and snapshot contents, including nested references; define deletion-event access without bypassing former exclusions.
implementation: Per-message/per-row fresh read-only authorization on Entry/App/Track/View; comment/attachment parent Entry gates
Scrub nested verification/reset/password fields from wire snapshots
Unknown resource snapshots withheld pending declared audience contracts
verification: test_access_perimeter_regressions.py: live revocation with Track and account scopes, audit and polling
test_invitation_mailbox_proof.py: real account event OTP hash withholding

findings.description: **Policy memoization omits inputs that change the decision.** Key contains subject/action/resource kind/id, but omits scope, entry type, tags, approval payload and policy revision. An allowed request can authorize another scope in the same context. The event subscription helper uses constant kind/id, so two Track scopes collide directly. `policy_engine.py:685`; `middleware/permissions_cache.py:15`; `event_subscription_registry.py:94`. Probes `test_policy_cache_ignores_scope_and_tags`, `test_event_subscription_decision_cache_crosses_track_scope`. Include complete immutable decision inputs; do not cache effect/approval creation. Start fresh, live authorization for each event.
implementation: Complete serialized Resource cache identity; no payload/effect memoization
verification: Scope/tag/type variations and distinct write payloads tested

findings.description: **Exclusion read fails open.** `_is_excluded_from_resource` catches an exception and returns False; an excluded user then inherits editor. `permissions.py:817`. Probe `test_exclusion_storage_error_allows_inheritance`. An indeterminate denial lookup must produce denied/unavailable, not “no exclusion.” Review all authority helpers for equivalent exception/default behavior.
verification: Authorized inheritance, exclusion denial and injected exclusion lookup failure

findings.description: **Point reads cross the bound workspace.** `ToolContext.get_entry/get` checks the user's resource role, but not the context's workspace or permitted App scope. A user authorized in workspaces A and B can read B through an A-bound facade; `get` labels the result as A. `hooks/registry.py:212,226`; inherited by `OperationContext`. Probe `test_facade_point_read_crosses_bound_workspace`. Resolve structural ownership and enforce execution workspace and App-declared reference authority for every facade method. This reproduces a scope breach for a principal authorized in both workspaces, not arbitrary-user access to B.

findings.priority_and_review_evidence: P0 / R locally; S/Q across workers
findings.description: **Revocation is not reliable across all caches.** Transfer leaves the former owner's warmed process role at owner until TTL expiry, enabling owner-only gates to remain open. Process cache defaults to 20 seconds and invalidation is in-memory per process. `ownership_transfer.py:16,86`; `permissions_process_cache.py:32,36,94`; `permissions.py:939`. Probe `test_ownership_transfer_leaves_warm_owner_cache`. Audit visibility/parent/lifecycle changes too. Durable authorization revisions must fence every worker and effect; local invalidation is only an optimization.

findings.priority_and_review_evidence: P0 / R, ordered race + stale issuer
findings.description: **Invitation authority and status can become stale.** A resource admin can issue an invite, lose all authority, and the invite still grants editor. Acceptance can observe pending, then complete after revoke has persisted. `invitations.py:371,437,477,517,763`. Probes `test_stale_inviter_still_confers_resource_grant`, `test_invite_accept_can_win_after_revoke`. Bind invitations to issuing authority and target workspace/policy revision; atomically claim pending status and materialize grants. Define authorized workspace-owner adoption of outstanding invitations.

**Workspace owners cannot govern all workspace resources.** A member's private App can be invisible to the workspace owner. Non-private inventory grants only commenter. Parent owner/admin caps at editor. `workspace_permissions.py:158`; `permissions.py:1030,1060`; I-ROLE-02; `test_app_owner_grant.py:151`. Probe `test_owner_governance_mismatch`. Introduce governance as a separately evaluated source of authority and revise the existing invariant deliberately.

**Selective creation grants can be self-assigned by workspace admins.** An admin with both creation flags False can PATCH its own membership to True. `api/workspaces.py:779,791,825`; `permissions.py:210,235`. Probe `test_workspace_admin_self_assigns_creation_rights`. If administrators are intentionally allowed to do this, false flags are advisory limits. Recommended: explicit delegation permissions and ceilings, with owner-controlled grant administration.

**Offboarding does not prevent re-entry.** Removing membership/grants does not create a suspension/removal embargo; a valid old share token adds guest membership again. Exclusions likewise lose to a redeemed direct grant. `workspace_departure.py:44`; `sharing.py:185`; `share_links.py:342`. Probes `test_removed_member_can_rejoin_via_existing_share_link`, `test_share_redeem_overrides_exclusion_and_link_revoke_retains_access`. Distinguish voluntary leave, resource removal and owner suspension; suspended users must not rejoin through old invitations/links.

**Ownership transfer is not an atomic ownership operation.** The service deletes owner/target collaborator edges before writing the replacement; a failed wire leaves no OWNS edge. Neither App nor Track transfer opens the graph transaction used by departure. Collaborator role owner passes delete but fails canonical OWNS-based transfer. `ownership_transfer.py:16,86`; `permissions.py:490,556`; `sharing.py:386`. Probes `test_transfer_write_failure_leaves_no_owns_edge`, `test_collaborator_owner_can_delete_but_cannot_transfer`. Separate canonical ownership from delegable role bundles; single-owner uniqueness, compare-and-swap transfer, receipts and cache fencing are required.

**Missing scope anchors disable the workspace membership gate.** If workspace lookup returns None, resolution continues with direct/inherited grants. Default workspace deletion unlinks resources and clears `workspace_id`, manufacturing this condition; it also conflicts with rooted inclusion. `permissions.py:879,1017`; `workspace_lifecycle.py:72,104`; `api/workspaces.py:523`. Probe `test_missing_workspace_anchor_allows_direct_grant`. Corrupt/unresolved containment must fail closed. Delete/archive/explicitly rehome resources in a validated transaction; never create unscoped survivors.

findings.priority_and_review_evidence: P1 / S; engine behavior R; reachability Q
findings.description: **Administering a policy subject is not a target-authority ceiling.** Policy CRUD checks that the caller owns/administers the agent/connector, but accepts wildcard scope/actions without checking all target authority. Engine matches an agent/connector Policy without intersecting the owner's current membership/resource authority. `api/policies.py:71,180`; `policy_engine.py:710`; `policy_registry.py:62`. Probe `test_policy_authority_scope_is_not_intersected` uses a synthetic wildcard Policy and confirms engine behavior, not an end-to-end connector exploit. Native resident dispatch commonly uses the human perimeter, so this is not evidence every resident call bypasses human access. Constrain issuance and intersect at every execution boundary.

**Declarative App functions are not fully delegable.** Human Policies are bypassed by the human default branch; operation `capability` is metadata while execution uses coarse `policy_action`. No complete user/group-to-App-action grant contract appears in the reviewed dispatcher. `policy_engine.py:701`; `app_operations/dispatch.py:59,153`; `schemas/app_operations.py:10`. Need namespaced actions, role bindings, bounded conditions, grant administration and identical enforcement across surfaces.

**Directory privacy differs by endpoint.** A viewer receives a reduced `/access`, but legacy `/apps/{id}/collaborators` returns other people and roles. Any guest can list the workspace member pool; public Track mention candidates can search graph Users. `sharing.py:959`; `api/apps.py:901`; `api/tracks.py:765,1076`; `api/workspaces.py:663`. Probe `test_viewer_legacy_collaborators_enumerates_other_people`. Define separately permission to read content, mention eligible people, and inspect access administration. Apply it consistently, with minimal user-field projections.

**Workspace avatar gate treats “none” as truthy.** `if not await can_access_workspace(...)` does not deny the nonempty string `"none"`; a non-member can fetch the logo. `api/workspaces.py:1312`. Probe `test_avatar_non_member_truthiness`. Low-sensitivity payload, clear IDOR-style gate defect. Use typed decisions or explicit role comparisons; audit other truthiness callers.
implementation: Compare WorkspaceRole to none before avatar storage reads
verification: Outsider denied without bytes read; authorized member bytes read

findings.description: **Roles and helper behavior disagree.** Viewer authors can edit/delete their own Entry through the author shortcut; I-ROLE-01 says viewer cannot mutate. The comparison is against the supplied principal ID, making graph/auth aliases another consistency concern. Direct viewer overrides stronger parent editor; resource owner and canonical owner differ. `permissions.py:581,1030`; I-ROLE-01. Probes `test_viewer_author_can_edit_own_entry`, `test_direct_viewer_suppresses_inherited_editor`. Specify author rights as an explicit capability/condition, canonicalize identity, and make precedence explicit.

**Governance lifecycle and evidence are incomplete.** No workspace ownership-transfer endpoint was found, although leave/account deletion messages require transfer. Workspace member changes live in API code with delete/recreate rollback, unlike the transactional departure service. Resource admins can issue invitations, but the resource invitation-revoke endpoint accepts only owner. Workspace changes often emit `scope=user:<actor>`, so the workspace owner lacks a complete workspace-governance audit view. Scope schemas even omit workspace as a ResourceKind despite workspace action branches. `api/workspaces.py:779,832,963`; `api/invitations.py:370`; `schemas/policy.py`; `api/policies.py:521`. Need canonical membership services, transfer/recovery, consistent scope types, workspace audit, bounded/paginated inventories and verified migration/repair.

findings.priority_and_review_evidence: P2 / S; module import and external reachability incomplete
findings.description: **The legacy generated-document list has the same truthiness pattern and insufficient row filtering.** `documents/generate.py:361` treats workspace role `"none"` as allowed. With no context Entry filter, the source returns all matching GeneratedDocument rows without per-document/context authorization; rows can contain resolved snapshots. Attempted service reproduction could not import the module because `template_lifecycle.py` imports missing `HAS_TEMPLATE_VERSION`. No external HTTP caller of this function was found. This is source-confirmed legacy debt, not a reproduced document-disclosure exploit. Reconcile/remove the inactive module, or repair its imports and authorization before exposing it. Treat this as a release blocker only if the affected module is included as a supported reachable surface; do not revive dead code merely to fix it.

findings.priority_and_review_evidence: P0 / R, read-operation dispatch; command replay S/Q
findings.description: **Operation replay can expose a now-excluded Entry.** A synthetic read handler checks the actual Entry permission and returns a validated Entry reference. After exclusion, a fresh operation invocation denies, but retrying the old idempotency key returns the original title/reference without rerunning the handler or reference authorization. App-level invocation permission still holds. `app_operations/dispatch.py::invoke_app_operation` returns `lookup_idempotent_result` before `build_result`; durable command replay similarly returns `execution.result`. Probe `test_read_operation_replays_entry_after_exclusion` exercises real policy, the warm in-process read-result cache and dispatch with only the App handler substituted. Clearing that cache did not reproduce persistent replay in this JsonDB fixture; do not infer cross-restart disclosure from this probe. Command/PostgreSQL replay is source-confirmed and still needs runtime qualification. Preserve effect idempotency while reauthorizing result disclosure; do not rerun an already committed mutation to regenerate its response.
implementation: Revalidate stored Entry dependencies at read and command response replay without rerunning committed effects
verification: Warm read replay allowed before exclusion and denied afterward, handler count unchanged

findings.description: **Accepted invitation metadata can overstate the resulting grant.** An existing viewer accepts an editor invitation; acceptance is saved as successful/editor while effective access remains viewer. `_materialize_invitation_grants` calls `ensure_edge`, which returns an existing edge without updating its attributes. Acceptance endpoints report the invitation's requested role rather than a verified effective result. Probe `test_accepted_invitation_reports_role_not_materialized`; `invitations.py::_materialize_invitation_grants`, `edge_upsert.py::ensure_edge`, `api/shared_with_me.py::post_accept_my_invitation`. This is a grant/receipt consistency defect, not an escalation. Define explicit existing-member/collaborator upgrade, no-op and conflict semantics, protected by version checks; never blindly overwrite newer grants.
